domain: Karst hydrogeology and cave survey — mapping unseen limestone drainage by injecting fluorescent tracer at a sinking stream and watching a pre-placed detector array at candidate springs; fast conduit flow versus slow diffuse matrix storage; non-detection as durable connectivity evidence; recovery ratios below one; sumps, chokes and dig faces as terminations; lead ledgers marking passages unpushed, pushed-and-closed or dug-out; and post-flood reorganization that expires an old connection map.
axioms: The network is opaque and mostly unconnected: the prior on any given candidate connection existing is low, so probe budget, not insight, is the binding constraint.
A non-detection is a hard-won, durable result about connectivity and must be recorded as carefully as a detection, or the same probe gets paid for twice.
The detector array must be fixed before injection; a result readable only after the fact is not a result.
The decision under contention is where to inject next, not what document to write; the primary output of probing is a change in allocation and frontier state.
The same system runs at incompatible speeds — hours in the conduit, years in the matrix — and an operation licensed on the fast layer must not rewrite the slow one.
Effort can leave the accounting entirely: recovery below one means some probing went somewhere never sampled, and that unrecovered cost belongs in every comparison.
Connection maps perish; a survey carries a grade and an age, and reorganization means old connectivity claims expire rather than accumulate.
Closing a lead is a real and valuable act: retiring a direction stops future budget from draining into it.
primitives: detector array and detection window (pre-registered success criteria)
positive trace / null trace (retained negative result)
conduit vs matrix (fast and slow pace layers)
lead ledger: unpushed / pushed-and-closed / dug-out (frontier state instead of an artifact)
sump, choke, dig face (stop rules and losing conditions)
survey grade (provenance carried by the map)
post-flood reorganization (expiry of a connectivity claim)
failure_mode: Weak on authority and provenance of individual claims: it grades the map, not the assertion, so it can let speculative material circulate ungraded and miss laundering paths at hard gate 4.
Biased toward state over artifact — may undervalue candidates whose real contribution is a legible, reviewable document a human consumer actually reads.
Assumes probes are cheap, reversible and independently interpretable; candidates whose probes are entangled, irreversible, or only meaningful in combination are outside its intuition.
Has no account of teaching, transfer, or propagation across contexts; a discovered conduit is local, so cross-context adaptation candidates get systematically underrated.
Frontier-ledger thinking can metastasize into unbounded bookkeeping, adding cognitive cost the charter explicitly prices as a criterion.
Its low prior on connectivity can shade into pessimism that suppresses generation — the safety-through-never-generating failure mode dressed as budget discipline.
Naturally geological rather than semantic: it can classify operations by cost and allocation effect while missing whether the epistemic transformation is genuinely distinct from Observe or Orient.
